from_notes: Kerala | Om Prakash Mathur (transferred from Sikkim)
from_notes_src: app notes 6:25 sub 1; Rocket CA 2026 Part 01 (src/current-affairs/rocket-ca-2026-01.txt) p.42
x: As of March 2025 both statements were true: Om Prakash Mathur had been Governor of Sikkim since 31 July 2024, and he earlier represented Rajasthan in the Rajya Sabha (2008-14, 2016-22). (Now: he was transferred as Governor of Kerala/Keralam on 12 Oct 2026; Sikkim's Governor is Dushyant Gautam.)
outdated: ⚠ Outdated: Om Prakash Mathur is no longer Sikkim's Governor — now Governor of Kerala/Keralam (orders 12 Oct 2026), with Dushyant Gautam as Governor of Sikkim (Rocket CA 2026 Part 01 p.42; daily CA 15 Oct 2026 p.1)
source: Praveen CA-360 May 2026 (src/current-affairs/praveen-ca360-2026-05-magazine.txt) p.17 (Sikkim Governor – Om Prakash Mathur); en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Om_Prakash_Mathur (Rajya Sabha from Rajasthan 2008-14, 2016-22, citing BJP Rajasthan / The Hindu); Rocket CA 2026 Part 01 p.42

from_notes: On January 24, 1950, the Constituent Assembly adopted the song Vande Mataram as national song. It has an equal status with Jana-gana-mana.
x: On 24 January 1950 the Constituent Assembly adopted Vande Mataram as the National Song, with equal status/honour with Jana Gana Mana (Rajendra Prasad's statement). It is not a UN/UNESCO heritage item, and no source credits Gandhi with a Gujarati translation, so 'none of these' is wrong.
source: PMF Modern History 03 (src/indian-history/pmf-modern-history-03.txt) p.102; NextGen Polity APPSC 08 (src/polity/nextgen-polity-appsc-08.txt) p.2; Rocket CA 2026 Part 02 p.133 (2026 Act gives it the same legal protection as the Anthem)

from_notes: in Carnatic raga Dheera Shankarabharanam, equivalent to Hindustani raga Bilawal
x: Hindustani Bilawal (all-natural, major-scale thaat) corresponds to the Carnatic 29th melakarta Dheera Shankarabharanam. Natabhairavi corresponds to Asavari, Kamavardhini (Pantuvarali) to Purvi/Puriya Dhanashri and Hanumatodi to the Bhairavi thaat.
source: app notes 6:26 sub 4; en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bilaval ('Bilaval is equivalent to the Carnatic melakarta Sankarabharanam')
evidence: PMF Art & Culture 02 (src/indian-history/pmf-art-culture-02.txt) p.36 (Bilawal listed; no Carnatic equivalent given)
